text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Assistant Minister Japheth Shamalla is beaten, stoned and ejected from the burial of slain student leader Solomon Muruli.
- Opposition parliamentarian Paul Muite accuses the Kenyan government of breaching most of the obligations endorsed by the Commonwealth to promote democracy.
- Opposition Democratic party calls for an impartial relief committee that will ensure emergency relief food reaches the intended beneficiaries.

- Leaders from Trans Nzoia district in the Rift Valley call for the sacking of local government minister Francis Lotodo for ignoring his collective responsibility and attacking his cabinet colleagues.
- Outspoken cleric Timothy Njoya of the Presbyterian Church of East Africa accuses the church in Kenya of condoning corruption.
- Tomi Makinen's hopes of a safari double are dashed after he suffers three punctures in the first competitive stage of the second leg in the ongoing 555 Safari Rally.
- Rangers from Masai Mara game reserve to be given weapons as part of the governments effort to boost security in the Park.
- Former World Champion Colin McCrae calls the shots in the second leg of the 555 Safari Rally in Kenya.
- Limuru legislator George Nyanja discloses that embattled Public Accounts Chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa received 12 million shillings in dubious circumstances from a leading bank in Nairobi.
- Uganda and Tanzania to merge their national airlines with Alliance Air.
- Worried by the increasing number of armed robberies, Kenya's banking industry is ready to pay up to get enhanced police protection.
- The Tanzanian government will set up a Petroleum Regulatory Agency as part of its efforts to liberalise the sector from July 1.
